name: Wallace Bowlingreen Clark
notable_stories: An active Republican campaigner even before he came of age, in 1896 he spoke against free silver in Missouri and was howled down in strongly pro-Bryan areas. In 1907 in Oklahoma he broke with his party to back adopting the constitution, and was nominated for Kay County attorney, having earlier received a similar nomination in Linn County.
milestones: Married Gertrude Adams (Clark) (m. 15 Sep 1898, Marceline, Missouri)
education: Educated in the district schools, the Salisbury Academy and the Keytesville Normal School; completed legal studies in the office of Major Mullins at Linneus
career: Attorney at law, practising in Marceline and Ponca City, OK
Taught school for seven years in Chariton and Ray counties before turning to law
Admitted to the bar January 13, 1899 before Judge John P Butler at Salisbury; practised law in Linn County for four years, then in Ponca, Oklahoma
sources: Descendants of Jose Pierre Adams, compiled by William W. "Bill" Allen (2 April 2011 edition)
notes: Siblings: Andrew J (Centerville, Iowa); Nancy J, wife of John J Rogers; William S. (Macon County, MO); John C. (Nebraska); Margaret, wife of AG Sterner; Mary, wife of S.L. Addis; Christiana, wife of EB Proctor; twins Edward and David [Bill Allen, Descendants of Jose Pierre Adams, line 4745]
